column1: # Applied symbol names for pure-psp-eu BOOT.BIN (image base 0x08804000).
# Not a reverse-engineering target (ADR-0009 defers Pure's simulation work);
# this is the result of a small, honest sweep for cross-binary matches
# against the documented psp-pulse-usa target, not independent derivation.
# See corroboration.md for method and what did NOT match.
# There is no `just` recipe for this set yet; run the script directly, with
# the program name and this file both given explicitly, against a bridge
# kind is `function` or `data`. Confidence below 70 gets a `_q` suffix
# Full sweep (2026-08-05): every function psp-pulse-usa/names.tsv documents,
# checked against this binary with bulk_fuzzy_match at threshold 0.8 and
# verified individually with diff_functions before renaming. See
# corroboration.md for the two collision-prone matches left out and why the
# _q-suffixed rows below still cleared the bar despite noisier diffs than
# String-anchor pass (2026-08-09). Independent of the fuzzy sweep above:
# these are named from the strings they reference, which survives the compiler
# READ string-anchors.md BEFORE running any address-based string tool against
# this binary. This import leaves code immediates UNRELOCATED while rebasing
# the data listing (data address = code constant + 0x08804000), so
# get_xrefs_to, find_undocumented_by_string and pointer byte-searches all
# report zero references for strings that are demonstrably in use - silently,
# with no error. The page documents the search that does work, and the
# low-half collision that makes searching an `addiu` without checking its
# Both rows below are browser middleware rather than game code, found while
# establishing the technique. Pure embeds a web browser; a large share of this
# binary is third-party middleware, which is a further explanation for the
# poor Pulse fuzzy-match rate. Deprioritised as a subject on user direction -
# the technique, not the browser, is the reusable result here.
# Front end. Resolves a "->"-separated element path against a screen, e.g.
# "Main Menu->Mode". The spine of the front end: every call site carries a
# literal element name, so naming outwards from here is cheap. See
# string-anchors.md for the fe:: class taxonomy the front-end XML is built
# from, and for the open question of which hash keys the child lists.
# Race box (2026-09-10). Decompiled directly, not corroborated from Pulse -
# see race-box-screens.md for the vtable-slot comparison and what is still
# open (the Phantom-model trigger, the record class that actually loads a
# mesh). Confirmed live in PPSSPP that both screens draw a real per-entity
# 3D preview, which the static reading alone had gotten wrong for
# DLC download completion check (2026-09-15), reached only once the Allegrex
# relocation fix (docs/ghidra/workflow.md) made get_xrefs_to work on this
# binary. See dlc-download-check.md for the full trace and what it does and
# does not settle about the pure-dlc-trailer-key-and-testbin-unknowns thread.
# The game's own XTEA cipher (2026-09-15), found chasing the same page's
# trailer-key lead. pure-usa's counterparts were not resolved - the Ghidra
# "Disk quota exceeded" bridge error), so only pure-eu is named here.
# The trailer's own RSA-shaped protection (2026-09-15), same investigation:
# DlcTrailer_ExtractKey reads the per-pack XTEA key straight out of the
# trailer at a fixed offset, once DlcTrailer_Validate's magic-string/digest/
# SDRM-tail checks pass. Bignum_Compare/Bignum_ModExp are the RSA-shaped
# modular-exponentiation machinery that recovers the trailer's plaintext -
# exact operand width unresolved, see dlc-download-check.md's own caveat.
# The same weapon-table, Disruptor and Bomb functions on this pressing
# (2026-09-15), transferred from psp-pure-usa by string anchor, constant
# per-subsystem shift and a per-function diff_functions check - see weapons.md
# for the method and the two _Init functions that carry a bigger discount.
# The dev/pub reel's hold duration (2026-09-23): a live PPSSPP breakpoint
# during a real cold boot confirmed both the call path and the 2.0s span
# directly. See devpub-reel-hold.md; the sibling init function and the
